Living Well / Resource directory

Help someone participate or contribute

Start with life

What would be useful?

Make it easier to listen, participate, preserve a story, or contribute something worthwhile.

The simpler starting point: Ask what would help. A direct conversation or small practical action can be more useful than introducing a new service.

Finish when: The person or project can use the contribution, and permissions and boundaries remain clear.

Choose by fit

Different tools, different jobs.

These are editorial comparisons based on public descriptions, not a ranking from hands-on tests. Choose one suitable route; using every option is not the goal.

Visual assistance and human help

Consider it when: You want to understand visual-assistance and volunteering options.

Check first: Follow the service’s guidance and the preferences of the person receiving help.

Access: Free personal-use app with setup/sign-in. Commercial offerings and optional hardware are separate.

Explore the personal-use app · Full context and source

Lookout: visual information on Android

Consider it when: A supported Android user wants to explore visual-information assistance.

Check first: Confirm important information; do not rely on descriptions alone for hazards.

Access: Free public instructions. Using Lookout needs a supported Android device, camera permissions, and any mode-specific requirements.

Open Lookout: visual information on Android · Full context and source

Live Transcribe: conversation access

Consider it when: Live text may help a willing conversation.

Check first: Discuss microphone use and how any history will be handled.

Access: Free public instructions. The feature needs a supported Android device and permissions; offline language support depends on the device.

Open Live Transcribe: conversation access · Full context and source

A question for a real conversation

Consider it when: You want a thoughtful starting question for a real conversation.

Check first: Talking is not automatic permission to record or publish.

Access: Free public question bank. Recording or uploading is not required to use it.

Browse Great Questions · Full context and source

By the People

Consider it when: You want to help make a public collection more usable.

Check first: Read the project’s actual transcription and contribution instructions.

Access: The introduction is free. Transcription can be done without registration; reviewing and tracking use an account.

Explore By the People · Full context and source

Zooniverse

Consider it when: You want to contribute to a citizen-science project.

Check first: Choose a project with instructions you can follow; your contribution is not independent proof of a conclusion.

Access: Projects and tutorials are public. Participation and account requirements depend on the project.

Explore Zooniverse · Full context and source

From choice to use

Keep the human purpose visible.

Respect the person before the process

Do not assume another person wants an app, recording, reminder, or public story. Useful assistance preserves their ability to choose.

Make a contribution the recipient can use

Follow project instructions or agreed formats. A smaller accurate contribution is better than a larger unreviewed one.

Keep connection larger than administration

A reminder or tool can support care, but it does not perform the listening or follow-through. Evaluate the effect on the other person, not just your own convenience.

Published as a selection path, not a personal field note. Source dates and access limits belong to each resource. No paid placement or affiliation is implied.
